claim.why_it_matters: In 15.91.3 VARIANCE returned values 1b and 1c, and in the closing 'where' sentence, the subscripts 1, 2, n and i on argument-1 are flattened into the name ('argument-11', 'argument-12', 'argument-1n', 'argument-1i'), so the definition of argument-1-sub-i and the equivalent arithmetic expression for VARIANCE read as references to differently named arguments.

verdict.reasoning: The 300-dpi render of PDF page 756 (printed page 732, §2014:15.91.3) shows argument-1 with lowered subscripts 1 and 2 in item b), subscripts 1 and n in item c), and subscript i in the 'where' sentence. page-756.md lines 29, 30, 36, 40 and 42 carry these as plain inline text: 'argument-11', 'argument-12', 'argument-11', 'argument-1n', 'argument-1i', with no <sub> markup. This is more than formatting. With the subscripts gone the tokens read as the names argument-11, argument-12 and so on, which are different metavariables, and the sentence that defines argument-1-sub-i as the ith argument loses its meaning. The claim quotes both sources accurately (it drops the '(FUNCTION SUM (' line of item c behind its '...', which does not affect the finding). One small addition: the defect also appears on line 36 (the first term of item c), which the claim covers only with its ellipsis.
verdict.corrected_description: §2014:15.91.3 VARIANCE returned values: subscripts on argument-1 (sub 1 and 2 in 1b; sub 1 and n in 1c; sub i in the 'where' sentence) are flattened to inline text in markdown lines 29, 30, 36, 40 and 42 ('argument-11', 'argument-12', 'argument-1n', 'argument-1i'). They should be argument-1<sub>1</sub> and so on.
